text:
Recent work supports separating evidence quality, explanation plausibility, and actual user choice. [ALERT (NAACL 2025)](https://aclanthology.org/2025.naacl-long.137/) evaluates recommendation explanations across 15 Amazon categories and 2,761 interactions; aggregated LLM judgments achieve 70% concordance with expert evaluation, leaving substantial disagreement. [Walk the Talk? (ICLR 2025)](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/b5ec50eb177908f21f78ed0d76ed525c-Abstract-Conference.html) demonstrates that plausible explanations can misrepresent influential evidence. Historical similarity therefore supports a relevance hypothesis, not proof of current intent or the model’s reasoning.

Suggested audit rubric, synthesized from these findings rather than an established validated instrument: **immediate choice** only with explicit current-intent evidence; **conditional usefulness** when documented item attributes match historical interests but usefulness depends on an unknown condition; **explicit mismatch** only with a cited contradiction; **insufficient evidence** when decisive facts are missing. Attach history references and title/description excerpts to every judgment; record conditions separately. Ownership, device compatibility, satisfied needs, and diversity/conformity traits remain unknown unless explicitly evidenced. Without direct user responses, annotations describe evidence-supported assessments, not observed user feedback.

For the twenty users, independently double-annotate lists, retain initial disagreements, report nominal Krippendorff’s alpha, raw agreement, and per-label confusion before adjudication. Validate automated judgments against these annotations. [Trust or Escalate (ICLR 2025)](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/file/08dabd5345b37fffcbe335bd578b15a0-Paper-Conference.pdf) supports calibrating escalation against human agreement; [Know Your Limits (2025)](https://aclanthology.org/2025.tacl-1.26/) reviews abstention evaluation. Report coverage alongside error among accepted judgments, with uncertainty intervals. This small audit cannot establish population-wide calibration; qualitative findings should remain separate from validation HR@10.
